clue.text: I subsist unhealthily with chips and junk food?

definitions.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing vessel, so food for a junk is fare eaten on board ship; the question mark flags the pun

indicators.note: eating unhealthily suggests these letters are in a bad, disordered state, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to living badly on chips and other junk food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhealthily' rearranges I SUBSIST and CHIPS together. 'junk food' looks like fast food, but a junk is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, dry rations once carried by sailors are, punningly, the food eaten aboard a junk.

clue.text: What's a lass dancing?

indicators.note: letters that are dancing are moving about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A simple question about what step a girl is doing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges A LASS, and the whole clue also asks what kind of dance she is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American dance style that a young woman might well be performing.

clue.text: Embrace with hot, very soppy love

parts.note: something hot is fashionable, or in

indicators.note: soppy means soft and limp, so the letters are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A sentimental lover goes for a hug, hot and very gushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soppy' signals the anagram of the last word. 'hot' means fashionable here, not warm.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace something is to include or comprise it, a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Plan for lifting huge pies

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting means the words are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: mega is slang for huge
tarts are pies

explanation.surface: A scheme for hoisting some enormous pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for lifting' turns MEGA TARTS upwards in this down entry, giving STRATAGEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning scheme or ruse is a synonym for a plan.

clue.text: Agreeing this month's record

parts.note: inst. (instant) is the old business-letter abbreviation for of this month
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record this month that everyone agrees on.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, short for 'instant', means 'of this month' in old commercial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in harmony with others, as marchers matching pace, is a common idiom for agreeing.

clue.text: About to leave friend picking up rubbish

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking up raises the words so they read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to part is to leave
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend about to go off is tidying up litter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' turns the two middle pieces upwards together, as the entry is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or empty talk is a common sense of rubbish.

clue.text: New Yorker's ticked off current score

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
to score something is to rate it

explanation.surface: A New York resident checks the latest score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticked off' is American slang for angry, hence the New Yorker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being angry is what Americans mean by ticked off, an idiom matched by the synonym.

clue.text: Sizzling porn star lacking shirt pocket

indicators.note: something sizzling is hot and agitated, so the letters are stirred up
lacking means a letter is taken away from the words

parts.note: T as in T-shirt

explanation.surface: A hot adult-film actor without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes T from PORNSTAR, and 'Sizzling' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the pouch worn at the front of a Scottish kilt, which serves as a pocket.

clue.text: Frame Wes?

parts.note: the instruction 'stitch' gives SEW and 'up' turns it upwards in a down entry, making the clue's word

explanation.surface: A one-word accusation that someone called Wes has been framed.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: SEW written upwards gives WES.
explanation.definitionFit: To frame someone is to fit them up falsely for a crime, British slang synonym.

clue.text: You can pull me when party's over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a revel is a party

explanation.surface: An invitation to make a move once the party has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses REVEL. 'pull' hints at seduction after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle or bar operated by pulling it, as in a signal box or machine.

clue.text: Wander casually towards Cornwall with a cop from home

parts.note: Cornwall is in the south-west of England, so heading there is SW
to cop is to catch, or nab
someone away from home is out

explanation.surface: Someone strolls off towards Cornwall with a police officer from back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a police officer but is the verb to catch. Cornwall is England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: To move about in an idle, showy way is a British idiom for wandering casually.

clue.text: Noah, Solomon and the rest take bit of tea in garden

parts.note: Noah and Solomon are Old Testament figures, so with the rest they are all OT men

indicators.note: a bit of the word means just its first letter

explanation.surface: Biblical patriarchs and kings stop for a cup of tea in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: OT is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented plot for growing vegetables is a kind of garden in Britain.

clue.text: Don't start to feel sorry for wader

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to regret is to feel sorry for

explanation.surface: An instruction not to begin pitying a wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the R from REGRET.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron, a long-legged bird that feeds in shallow water.

clue.text: Ministers showing cold dislike, except for a Liberal

indicators.note: except for means these letters are left out

parts.note: an allergy is a strong dislike

explanation.surface: Government ministers display frosty disdain, all but one Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for' drops the A and L named in the clue. 'Ministers' looks political, but these are church ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: Church ministers collectively, priests and vicars, make up the body of ordained people.

clue.text: Where you can call 100 too old

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
overage means too old

explanation.surface: An unclear grumble about a 100-year-old being too old to phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call 100' reads like dialling a number; 100 is just C.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile network's area of signal is where phone calls can be made.

clue.text: Nick and Henry's bird

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry
a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Two men, Nick and Henry, share a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Half-inch is Cockney rhyming slang: half-inch = pinch, meaning to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang for pinch, which like nick means to steal.

clue.text: Guaranteed to make teacher look silly about oxygen

parts.note: to make someone look silly is to fool them

indicators.note: about means going around something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a prof (professor) is a teacher
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A sure-fire way to embarrass a chemistry teacher over oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the oxygen symbol inside the teacher; 'to make' is link padding around the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot fail, however careless the user, is effectively guaranteed to work.

clue.text: As carriages on railway lines

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
a train is a line of railway carriages

explanation.surface: Like rail carriages running on tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' looks like railway lines but means lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza of four lines of verse is what lines here refers to.

clue.text: Vet (not mouse), removing tails with toxin …

indicators.note: removing tails means the last letter of each word is dropped

explanation.surface: A vet examining a non-mouse animal docks tails using poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of each of Vet, not and mouse: VE + NO + MOUS. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carrying poison, like a snake bite, is described this way.

clue.text: New leg added to stump

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
plus means added

explanation.surface: A new leg is fixed onto an amputee's stump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stump' looks like a limb or cricket stump but is the verb to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To stump someone is to baffle or perplex them, a synonym.

clue.text: … interviews second-in-command about animal surgery

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a VP, vice-president, is second-in-command
an ox is an animal
an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: The deputy is questioned about veterinary operations, continuing the vet theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the animal inside the deputy's abbreviation. Vox pop is short for vox populi, voice of the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick opinion interviews with members of the public in the street are known by this term.

clue.text: Poor nun disfigured herself, perhaps

indicators.note: disfigured means spoilt in shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An unfortunate nun has injured her own face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disfigured' rearranges POOR NUN. 'perhaps' marks herself as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Herself is an example of a word that stands in place of a noun.

clue.text: Hold tight and pedal

definitions.meaning: the foot control in a car that disengages the engine

explanation.surface: An instruction to grip hard and cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to grip and the car's foot-operated control.

clue.text: Was in charge of church and farm

parts.note: ran means was in charge of

explanation.surface: Someone managed both a church and a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cattle farm, especially in North America.

clue.text: Job is a crock of shite

indicators.note: a crock is a broken-down wreck, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that some job is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a crock of' rearranges SHITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Job is criminal slang for a robbery, as in an inside job.

clue.text: Earl wearing coat over husband's only ring

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters run backwards
wearing means one piece is inside another, as a body inside clothing

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's coat
H is the abbreviation for husband
one means only, as in the one person

explanation.surface: An aristocrat in a fur coat asks after a husband's single ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts E in PELT; 'over' reverses that to TELEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is to call them up on the phone.

clue.text: Provide space as required

parts.note: an en is a printer's space of half an em
due means as required or owed

explanation.surface: An instruction to supply room as needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow or furnish someone with a quality, a literary synonym.

clue.text: 10-4 in bold

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: gallant means brave or bold
IV is the Roman numeral for 4

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that reads like a radio call sign, 10-4.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 points to 10 across, SWAN ABOUT. '10-4' looks like radio jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam about for pleasure is to wander casually, the meaning of 10 across.

clue.text: Round and hollow, like an eggshell

parts.note: O is round in shape
a void is a hollow, an empty space

explanation.surface: A description of an egg's shell, round and empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-shaped is the literal meaning of the word.

clue.text: Don't decide to put down the receiver!

parts.note: to sit on something is to suppress it, put it down
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: An instruction to hang up the phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiver' looks like a phone handset but is a fence for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying neutral and refusing to take a side is an idiom for not deciding.
